items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Harry Carney was there longer than anybody... most of us would know

ctx.x: Did the – how much of that band was on the paper? How much was in those guys heads?

All of it was on the paper originally, when he wrote it, and most of it was remembered by the – over a period of years, except that Harry Carney was there longer than anybody, but he always got out every piece of music, every night, that was being played – every night, every piece of music. And though I’m sure that 99% of it he knew, like most of us would know, but there’s some things you – there’s a couple of little passages in there that are intricate, that you would need to see the music on from time to time.
I asked this a little bit different, when I asked you to go back again – did you learn anything as far as technique or in the jazz idiom in that band?
